story: At 7:17 on this sunny Saturday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is bent over his workbench at home, testing wiring for the light strings and sound system without mounting anything on his golf cart yet. Donna is at her kitchen table with the club calendar, penciling in the Halloween parade and costume contest and confirming her one o'clock court time with Gary. Across the way, Hal is watching Magnolia Loop through his binoculars, counting flamingos and noting any cart modifications he spots, while Rosa, cheerful as ever, has started baking and bagging treats for tonight's trick-or-treaters.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Pre-assemble the light strings and test the sound system wiring on the bench, nothing mounted on the cart
Donna (donna club calendar): Look over today's club calendar, confirm the one o'clock court time with Gary, and pencil in the Halloween parade and costume contest
Hal (hal binoculars): Scan Magnolia Loop for visible flamingos and cart modifications, then log counts
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Start baking and bagging the Halloween treats for tonight's trick-or-treaters

gary.thought_process: It's 7:17 AM on parade day and I'm home alone. The Architectural Review application still isn't signed off, so under L-01 I can't mount anything visible from the street, and the cart stays in the garage. But the wiring sketches and clamp list I can do something about. The sound system can be tested indoors and quietly, and it's well after 7 AM so L-03 isn't an issue. Best use of this hour is bench work on the workbench so everything's ready the second approval comes through, without breaking any rules.

parameters.content: Pre-assemble the light strings and test the sound system wiring on the bench, nothing mounted on the cart

donna.thought_process: It's 7:17 AM on Halloween morning and I'm home alone. Gary and I have our one o'clock court date today before the parade, and I'm still the social chair of three clubs, so there's plenty to organize. The club calendar is right here. Before I head out to the Loop, I should check what's on it today, Halloween events, club meetings, and our court time, so I can plan my day and keep my place at the center of things.

parameters.content: Look over today's club calendar, confirm the one o'clock court time with Gary, and pencil in the Halloween parade and costume contest

hal.thought_process: It's early, I'm home, and nobody's around. My memories say I headed to Magnolia Loop last tick, but I'm in my house now. Parade is tonight and my immediate goal is to keep an eye on the Loop for violations: Gary's cart mods, Donna's flamingos. Binoculars are right here, and the notebook is where I log things. Best use of this hour is a quiet morning survey of the street from the porch, tallying ornaments and checking the cart before the crowds and decorations show up. Fair is fair; I want facts in the notebook before I say a word to the committee.

parameters.content: Scan Magnolia Loop for visible flamingos and cart modifications, then log counts

rosa.thought_process: It's early Saturday morning, Halloween, and I'm home. I already confirmed my shift schedule is clear for tonight, so there's no need to check it again. The treats for the kids are the next thing on my list, and I'm looking forward to seeing Gary and Donna at the Loop tonight. The kitchen is the right place to start baking and prepping candy bags before the day gets away from me.

parameters.content: Start baking and bagging the Halloween treats for tonight's trick-or-treaters

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
